title: Determine if Two Strings Are Close
summary: Two strings are considered close if one can be transformed into the other by swapping any two of its characters or by replacing all occurrences of one character with another character and vice versa.
statement: Two strings are considered close if one can be transformed into the other by swapping any two of its characters or by replacing all occurrences of one character with another character and vice versa. Return true if the strings are close, and false otherwise.
constraints: Swaps can reorder freely; global exchanges can reassign existing character frequencies only among characters present in both strings.
hints: Swaps remove positional information; global exchanges permute counts among the same character set.
Compare the set of present characters and the sorted multiset of their counts.
Build two Counters and require equal keys plus equal sorted values.
Both invariants are necessary, and swaps plus frequency-label exchanges can realize any arrangement satisfying them.
editorial: Both invariants are necessary, and swaps plus frequency-label exchanges can realize any arrangement satisfying them.

tests.explanation: Reordering alone transforms one string into the other.
Different lengths and frequency multisets cannot be transformed.
